plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Allfrey, Faulkner & Mirsky (May 1964, PNAS 51: 786–794) histone acetylation transcription chart & Holliday & Pugh (24 January 1975, Science 187: 226–232) / Riggs (1975) semi-conservative CpG DNA methylation inheritance diagram shows 2 metres of DNA packed into a 6-um nucleus on nucleosome spools and DNMT1 copying 5-methylcytosine (5mC) tags from the parental CpG strand onto the newly replicated daughter strand.

teach_overlay.scale: copying methyl tags during cell division works like tracing carbon paper — when the two DNA strands unzip to replicate, the old strand still wears its methyl sticky notes, and a maintenance enzyme immediately stamps matching sticky notes onto the fresh copy
